result.proved: A Jordan contour enclosing exactly a connected edge subtree of the ray-separated sheet tree acts as one full cycle on that subtree's incident sheet block and fixes the complement. A moved-block average complete-lift bound at most two then solves the target conditionally by the fixed-block theorem.
result.candidate_evidence: Pinned degree-6 and degree-9 near-Fekete witnesses admit circles wholly inside the unit value disk enclosing exactly their two and three admissible critical values. Numerical continuation gives moved cycles of sizes three and four with means about 1.84327 and 1.63875, while the largest individual lift exceeds two in both rows.
result.human_understanding_delta: The hard witnesses do not require circling inadmissible branch values. Their admissible critical values already form a promising partial cluster, and averaging on its moved cycle is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
result.verification_state: PASS ordinary exact conditional topology proof; PASS deterministic bit-pinned continuation with critical-value inclusion/exclusion margins, value-disk clearance, cycle-size checks, and coarse/fine drift guards
result.claim_boundary: The witness length rows are floating-point candidate evidence without interval enclosures and are not rigorous instance proofs. No universal partial-cluster average bound is proved; unrestricted Erdős 1041 remains open.
result.surviving_frontier: Bound or interval-certify the partial-cluster moved-block average, then connect failure to a complementary Bergman merge-node certificate.
